scenes.body: That's +2 basis points on the day and -37 bp over the past month. (100 bp = 1 percentage point.)

scenes.headline: Today's yield curve
scenes.body: The curve slopes **upward**: longer loans pay more, which is the normal shape. The 10-year minus 3-month spread is +0.86 points.

scenes.headline: The 10-year's path
scenes.label: 10-year · 3 months
scenes.note: Rising yields raise borrowing costs for mortgages and companies, and make bonds more competitive with stocks.

scenes.question: Based on today's numbers, is the yield curve (10-year minus 3-month) inverted?
scenes.explain: The 10-year is at 4.86% vs. 4.00% for 3-month bills.

scenes.headline: India Sensex leads global markets, Japan Nikkei lags
scenes.body: US stocks don't trade in a vacuum. Here's how major markets abroad finished their latest session.

scenes.body: Asia trades first, then Europe, then the US. A sell-off overseas can set the mood for Wall Street's open, and big US companies earn a large share of their sales abroad.

scenes.headline: Could the AI bubble burst after Democrats' midterms sweep? - The Latest
scenes.body: Global tech stocks have plunged after the Democrats’ victory in the US midterm elections, with fears of a slowdown in AI development.

scenes.headline: The details
scenes.body: Major tech corporations including Apple, Tesla and Nvidia shed about $1tn in a single trading session. Is this stock market jitters, or a sign the AI bubble might be about to burst?

scenes.body:
AI spending has been one of the market's biggest themes, so chip and cloud news can move the heaviest stocks in the index.
